## TL;DR

Shots now carry a width. A declared shot can set `viewport` to `phone` (390x844), `tablet` (820x1180) or `desktop` (1280x800). An undeclared web target is captured at phone and desktop, so a mobile QA pass gets a phone frame next to the desktop one. Tablet is only captured when a shot declares it. Every web caption names its size, and unknown viewport names are rejected with the list of valid ones. This session's handoff failure was not in the shot code: two WebKit responsive tests (`checks-live-run-responsive`, `checks-releases-data-responsive`) failed at 375 px because the Vite test server re-hashed its dependencies while the page was loading. I fixed that in the test harness only, and the layout assertions are unchanged.

## Work and rationale

The task said the CLI already accepted `--viewport`, and that declared shots had no width field. Reading the code showed that was only half true. `src/core/shot-plan.ts` already had `viewportWidth` and `viewportHeight` on a declared shot, and the capture loop already honoured them per entry. What was missing was a named preset, so an engineer had to remember 390 and 844 by heart. The automatic fallback was the real gap: it emitted one entry per web target, always at the 1280x800 default.

I kept the numeric fields as the stored truth and added `viewport` as a spelling of them. The parser maps the preset to `viewportWidth` and `viewportHeight`, so capture, collapse key, plan fingerprint and reuse rule needed no change. A shot that names a preset and also gives a mismatching width or height is rejected, because the two would disagree about what gets captured.

The fallback change lives in `buildCapturePlan`. Each web target now yields one entry per fallback viewport, phone then desktop. A command target still yields one entry, since its command renders its own image. Declared shots never fan out.

Captions carry the size through provenance. `provenanceCaption` appends it as `· phone 390x844`, so the existing caption paths pick it up without per-caller edits. For a declared shot with no `viewport`, the caption names the default it really gets, `desktop 1280x800`.

On the CLI, `repoos shot --viewport WxH` pins the automatic capture to one size. Without the flag, `repoos shot` fans out to phone and desktop, and the help text says so. Docs: `docs/agent-ui-and-preview-conventions.md` records the viewport behaviour and capture-time cost, `docs/previews.md` and `user-docs/review-and-close-out.md` describe the caption and fan-out, and `user-docs/cli.md` documents the `viewport` key.

Handoff failure, this session. The gate's WebKit tests failed on the 375 px cases. I reran them locally and found two separate causes.

1. The default 5 s page and test budgets are too short for a first cold WebKit run through Vite. The Releases file had no per-test timeout at all. I raised the page default to 30 s in both files and gave the Releases cases a 60 s test timeout, matching the live-run file.
2. The real stall was the Vite dependency optimizer. Vite scans only `index.html` for dependencies by default, so `vue` and `pinia` were discovered during the first page load. That re-hashed the optimized bundle, and the page's already-requested `vue.js` and `pinia.js` came back `504 (Outdated Optimize Dep)`. The view never mounted and the test waited out its budget. I confirmed this with temporary console and response logging, which I removed afterwards. The fix is `optimizeDeps.entries` in each test server, pointing at its fixture entry and store stub, so dependencies are bundled before the first page request.

## Approaches tried

I first considered widening `maxAutoShots` to limit the fan-out. That cap is a per-command count, and reusing it for web viewports would have silently dropped the phone capture whenever a target had several captures. I left the cap alone.

I also considered a `[shot] viewports` setting in `repoos.toml`. The task says never to touch `repoos.toml`, and a user-facing setting would need a Settings control. Fixed sizes met the acceptance criteria, so I left configuration out.

For the flaky WebKit tests, I first treated them as timing alone and only raised timeouts. The 375 px cases still failed with a 30 s stall, which did not fit a slow start. Sequential runs failed too, so cross-file contention was ruled out. The diagnostic logging showed the 504s, and that changed the fix.

## Challenges and blockers

The branch is 86 commits behind `main`. Its shot changes were already in earlier WIP checkpoints, and this session started from them. I did not merge main in this session. The two responsive test files are identical to main, so the fix does not depend on that merge.

The shot-plan tests pinned the single-entry fallback in several assertions. Those changed on purpose, and I updated each to the two-entry shape and the sized caption rather than pinning the old output. The shot-plan and viewport suites pass: 101 tests across two files.

Nothing needed a human step. Still unverified: the phone frame's visual result has not been looked at, because I did not run a headless capture of a real page in this session. The handoff capture honouring a viewport per shot is a one-line read of `captureEntryPage`, and no test drives a browser through it. Someone should look at a phone capture once a preview is requested.

The scoped gate (`REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check`) passed end to end, including the remote validation run. All nine live-run WebKit cases and all three releases WebKit cases passed in that run.

## Key learnings

The provenance object is a good place for a fact every caller must render. Making `provenanceCaption` the single renderer reached every caption path without touching each call site.

The existing `viewportWidth`/`viewportHeight` fields were already the right model. A named preset is only a spelling of them, so no capture code changed.

A WebKit test that fails only on the first page of a file, with a long stall and no layout error, is more likely a dependency-optimizer state problem than a slow machine. Raising the timeout hid the stall without fixing it. The 504 "Outdated Optimize Dep" response in the browser console was the clear signal, and only logging the page's network and console showed it.
